title: Forgiving everyone
hookLine: an ordinary man, promised Paradise, who did nothing special except sleep with no grudge
tomorrow: why did someone stay behind in Mecca on the night of the escape?

lines: ASLEEP THE MOMENT HE LIES DOWN.
A MAN OF PARADISE WALKS IN.
cards: Some people fall asleep the moment their head hits the pillow, and it can feel deeply unfair.

In a report in Musnad Ahmad, the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ tells his companions that a man of Paradise is about to walk in, and an ordinary man of the Ansar walks in. A young companion, Abdullah ibn Amr, wants the secret.
He finds a reason to stay at the man's house and watch. He sees nothing special: no all-night prayers. Just a man who remembers Allah when he turns over in bed, and sleeps.

teach.b: So Abdullah asks him outright. The man says: it's only what you saw, except that I keep no grudge in my heart against any Muslim, and I don't envy anyone for the good Allah has given them.
Abdullah says: that is what got you there. Forgiving everyone isn't a speech.
It's a nightly putting-down, and it doesn't wait for the other person to go first.

teach.h: YEARN YE NOT TO BE FORGIVEN?
teach.b: The report names fellow Muslims; the Qur'an's line on forgiving reaches wider, in Pickthall's words: "let them forgive and show indulgence. Yearn ye not that Allah may forgive you?"
Now the week comes back as one road. Committed: a small rule, signed. A pilgrimage: leave, circle, stand, return.
Just passing: a light bag. Loves to meet him: a meeting you get ready for.
Think well: hope leads at the end. What continues: good that outlives you. And the lightest thing to carry into sleep is nothing at all.

how: Some Muslims make a habit of forgiving everyone before they sleep, pointing to this report in Musnad Ahmad; Qur'an 24:22 is often recited as a reason to forgive.

o: agreeing that whatever someone did was all right
asking each person you've hurt to forgive you
letting go of grudges and envy, every night

games.q: the week's lines — tap the pairs.

s: in the report, the man of Paradise prayed all night
Abdullah saw nothing special. the man's secret: no grudge, no envy.
forgiving in Islam means pretending it never happened
the practice is setting the grudge down; nothing says you must pretend or fully trust again.
Qur'an 24:22 asks: yearn ye not that Allah may forgive you?
let them forgive and show indulgence.

games.q: you keep replaying a coworker's rude comment every night, and it's costing you sleep. what does the man of Paradise's habit point to?
o: set the grudge down before sleep, every night it comes back.
wait to forgive until she apologizes; then let it go.
pray longer at night so the good outweighs the anger.
games.why: he did nothing special except keep no grudge in his heart. forgiving here is a nightly putting-down, not a reward for an apology.

practice: Close your eyes and bring to mind one person you're still holding something against, even a little. Breathe out slowly and, for this one breath, set it down; you don't have to call them or pretend it didn't happen.
If it comes back, set it down again.

wordCard.voice: Forgiving everyone: letting go of grudges and envy, every night, so you can sleep with a clear heart.

orig.note: Arabic: pardon, letting a wrong go; the Qur'an uses this root in 24:22.

carryVoice: Two words for the pillow tonight: no grudge, set down before you sleep. Sleep well, and see you tomorrow.

sources.ref: Musnad Ahmad 12697 (from Anas): a man of the Ansar is called a man of Paradise; Abdullah ibn Amr stays with him and finds nothing special except that he holds no grudge against any Muslim and envies no one

sources.q: let them forgive and show indulgence. Yearn ye not that Allah may forgive you?
